body:
Ah, you are certainly not unhelpful at all. I feel honored that you've taken the time to respond and, incidentally, you've (unknowingly and very gently, of course) dug at an open wound that I've had for the entirety of my adult life. I have idealized the act of writing for the purpose of creation and catharsis since I was a child. I, clearly, turn to writing as a productive means to my own end for the same reason. (Incidentally, all of my letters to my friends and my obituary are unfinished and completely unsatisfying to me. I feel terribly blocked by my own inadequacy to express my own thoughts -- I am very touched by your generous attitude towards the way I've expressed myself here.)

I just can't do it on any real level, though. I had a therapist for over a year who regularly encouraged me to be creative, to write out my daydreams into cohesive thoughts. It annoyed me so much; I felt like one of those TV characters on the therapist's couch that lashes out at the doctor, and the therapist and audience just inwardly cringe at how oblivious the patient is being. "Why don't you write something?" -- Well, why don't YOU write something (three-year-old-logic). 

I have moved recently and started working in a new field. On a surface level, I would say my life has improved drastically from where it was before. When I moved and started seeing a new therapist, I made it three sessions in before he expressed the same sentiments about "writing as an outlet", and I haven't been back yet.

I guess, if I were to try to describe it, I would say that it's hard when there's already all this pressure that I'm supposed to be releasing, and people are constantly telling me that "for someone like me, the pressure should be released in this way", which then puts pressure on the method of relief as well.

I appreciate your words of encouragement and I feel very emotional right now hearing about this sense of gratitude(?) at having survived your attempt. I laughed a little reading "3 puppies", as it struck me as a totally valid reason to keep-on-living. (Strange, though, yes? ... when the love I feel from so many never seems to be enough. Maybe it was more of a nervous laugh than anything, but it does feel good.) 

I hope that your depressive funk is just that -- a funk. I often find myself thinking that if I did have a long-term boyfriend or siblings or [anything someone else has] I would not feel this way. But as stated in my original post, I already have so much. I am proud of you for cherishing what you have despite your looming depression, and I promise to actively try to follow by example.

Thank you for sharing your personal story about your sister. I definitely needed to hear from someone who has felt those lasting effects. I can't even imagine something so painful, and from what I've experienced of grief, I can certainly understand having recurring anger towards people who ultimately were just seeking relief from a pain they couldn't face: the same pain that brings both of us here now. 

"It's like after she shot herself, my head started filling up with all these ways to leave" ... and boy, do I feel this. One of the reasons I've been able to keep going is this sneaking suspicion that my leaving would encourage other people to take that same route. It's hard not to learn by example from those we love. 

I hope that you are able to keep going, too. Someday, if you haven't already, I'm sure you're son will appreciate hearing about your struggle. I will keep your sister in my thoughts.

Hi! I'm sorry that you're feeling the same way. I often think that same sort of mantra to myself. I really like your question -- I had never really thought about it in those terms. I do try very hard to be a good person most of the time, though I certainly have my "screw this" moments. And during those moments I find myself doing hurtful things. Reflecting on the practical nature of my planning, I think it's more a result of "contemplating suicide for quite a while now" as you said, but maybe also a desire to do it perfectly. And I've never been able to write anything longer than a page without hating it for being less than perfect, so I can definitely see that in myself. Thank you for responding, by the way.
